Who to watch

Brown leaders (2026, through their last game)

  • Passing: #15 James Murphy — 145/230, 1562 yds, 3 TD, 9 INT
  • Rushing: #2 Matt Childs — 85 car, 351 yds, 6 TD
  • Receiving: #2 Matt Childs — 38 rec, 430 yds, 1 TD
  • Tackles: #10 Max Malo — 73
  • Sacks: #0 Ike Odimegwu — 3.5

Brown comes in off its first Ivy win: down 31-17 to Cornell in the fourth quarter on Oct. 24, it scored the last 21 points, tied it on the final play of regulation with Matt Childs' 9-yard catch and won 38-31 in overtime on Childs' 25-yard run. Childs was named Ivy League Offensive Player of the Week; James Murphy, without a touchdown pass all season, threw three. The defense allows 16.2 points a game, seventh in FCS, and Max Malo leads the country with 12.2 tackles a game. A win would give Brown back-to-back Ivy home wins for the first time since 2016 (Brown game notes via BVM Sports; Penn Athletics; ESPN).

Penn leaders (2026, through their last game)

  • Passing: #12 Miles Teodecki — 85/156, 763 yds, 4 TD, 3 INT
  • Rushing: #12 Miles Teodecki — 45 car, 194 yds, 1 TD
  • Receiving: #87 Mason Page — 26 rec, 333 yds, 2 TD
  • Tackles: #15 Zach Darche — 58
  • Sacks: #2 Joey Holliday — 4

Penn is in its first season under head coach Rick Santos, the program's 150th. Freshman quarterback Miles Teodecki hurt his knee against Howard and came back to throw two touchdown passes in a 24-21 win over Yale on Oct. 23, when Penn intercepted Dante Reno four times and shut Yale out after halftime. The defense is the story: second in FCS in total defense (270.2 yards a game) and first in pass defense (149.0), with only 14 touchdowns allowed (Penn Athletics, Oct. 29; The Philadelphia Inquirer).

From the press

At Coppell High School in Texas, Odimegwu played both running back and defensive end; as a senior he scooped up a fumbled snap on a Hebron extra-point try and ran it back for two points in a 43-35 Heroes Night win. His Brown bio credits him with the 2022 District 6A Defensive MVP award and first-team all-area honors.

  • As a senior defensive end for Coppell High School on Heroes Night (Coppell 43, Hebron 35), he recovered a fumbled snap on a Hebron point-after attempt and returned it for two points; quoted afterward: "I wanted to be in the endzone." (The Sidekick / Coppell Student Media, Oct. 22, 2022)
  • Earlier in his Coppell career he lined up at running back, opening the scoring with a two-yard touchdown run in a homecoming win over the Wildcats. (The Sidekick / Coppell Student Media (game story, year not shown in index))
  • Named 2022 District 6A Defensive MVP and first-team all-area as a senior at Coppell, per his Brown roster bio. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2025)

  • In 2025 he ran 137 times for 517 yards and eight touchdowns (ESPN) and earned Second Team All-Ivy League honors (WJAR Turn to 10). (ESPN player page; WJAR Turn to 10, 2025-26)

  • Graduated as Windermere Prep's record holder in 12 statistical categories, including total yards (3,198), career rushing yards (2,351), career points (244) and total touchdowns (39); also played lacrosse. From the press

Mason Walters won a game with his very first college kick, a 45-yard field goal at Stonehill in 2025. Against Columbia on Oct. 16, 2026, he made a 52-yarder in the first quarter, but his rushed 51-yard try on the final play fell just short in a 28-27 loss.

  • His 45-yard field goal on his first collegiate attempt was the game-winner at Stonehill in September 2025, giving Penn its first win of the season. (The Daily Pennsylvanian, 2025)
  • Kicked a 52-yard field goal in the first quarter against Columbia at Franklin Field on Oct. 16, 2026, set up by a Ty Cortes interception. (The Philadelphia Inquirer, 2026 (Conor Smith, Oct. 17, 2026))
  • His rushed 51-yard attempt on the final play against Columbia fell just short, and Penn lost 28-27 after leading 24-7 at halftime. (The Philadelphia Inquirer, 2026 (Conor Smith, Oct. 17, 2026))

The series: Brown vs. Penn

All-time: Penn leads 65-26-2; Saturday is the 94th meeting. Penn has won 8 of the last 10 and the last two, and is 20-16-1 in Providence (Penn Athletics, Oct. 29).

Last year, Friday, Oct. 31, 2025 — Halloween, under the lights at Franklin Field (ESPNU) — Penn 28, Brown 21. Penn led 21-7 at the half and ran for 231 yards to Brown's 33. Murphy threw for 360. Brown's touchdowns included one thrown by a receiver, Najih Rahman to Pearson Hill.

Penn scores: 1st Donte West 1 yd run (0-7); 2nd Bisi Owens 9 yd pass from Liam O'Brien (7-14); 2nd Sean Williams Jr. 1 yd run (7-21); 3rd West 1 yd run (14-28). Mason Walters all four kicks.
Brown scores: 1st Ty Pezza 44 yd pass from James Murphy (7-7); 3rd Pearson Hill 4 yd pass from Najih Rahman (14-21); 4th 1:41 Trevor Foley 14 yd pass from Murphy (21-28). Drew Crabtree all three kicks.

Game day

The stadium

Richard Gouse Field at Brown Stadium opened October 24, 1925, before 27,000 at the dedication. Capacity 20,000; the record crowd was 33,000 (Colgate, Thanksgiving 1932). FieldTurf since 2021, named for donor Richard I. Gouse '68. Ivy championship teams: 1976, 1999, 2005, 2008.

Saturday

  • Halloween kickoff at noon. Last year's meeting was also on Halloween.
  • Streaming on ESPN+: Scott Cordischi (play-by-play), John Anderson (analyst), Nick Coit (sideline), per Penn Athletics.
  • Promotions and parking were not in any preview this tool could read; check brownbears.com before you go.

Sources & notes

Built Oct. 24; final refresh Friday evening, Oct. 30, 2026, for offline reading. Rosters, bios and photos: brownbears.com and pennathletics.com (Penn photos through the schools' content network). Statistics: ESPN's public box scores, summed per player. Schedules, standings, team yardage and the line (DraftKings): ESPN. Game notes: Penn Athletics' preview (Oct. 29); Brown Athletics' notes as summarised by BVM Sports (Oct. 29); Philadelphia Sports Now (Oct. 30); Brown Athletics' Cornell recap and Ivy honour (Oct. 24 and 26). Penn storylines: The Philadelphia Inquirer. Last meeting: ESPN box score and Wikipedia's 2025 Brown season page. Stadium: Wikipedia. Forecast: National Weather Service, Oct. 30.

Caveats: Brown's own release could not be read directly (its site refuses this tool), so Brown's notes come through BVM Sports' summary; promotions and parking were not found. Another book has Brown -2.5. Murphy's passing yards are summed from box scores (1,562); Penn's preview gives 1,532. Brown bios are the official roster line plus a sourced press search. Numbers from unverified sources were left out.
